subject: Standby region scenarios, RTO/RPO mapping and fallback procedures
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@sentryfin.com>
To: rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: RFP follow-up: regional standby / RTO-RPO mapping request

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement team has moved us to the technical deep-dive phase of the RFP. We have three prioritized scenarios we need your written responses for:

1) Single-region outage where active region loses network/connectivity (expected switchover to standby in another region).
2) Partial compute degradation (50% GPU capacity) in primary region during peak traffic.
3) Cloud provider AZ-level storage degradation with read-after-write implications.

For each scenario we need: expected RTO and RPO (numbers and explanation of what is included), estimated customer-visible downtime for long-running streaming requests, which components require manual intervention during failover, and whether write-before-commit semantics are preserved across regions.

Can you return a mapping table and any runbook excerpts? Procurement would like this by EOD Tuesday PST.

Regards,
Daniel
Infrastructure Ops – Sentry Financial

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: regional standby / RTO-RPO mapping request

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear breakdown. Attaching a concise RTO/RPO matrix and a short architecture diagram that maps our standby activation paths. High level answers up front so you can share immediately:

- Scenario 1 (full region network failure): Typical automated failover path gives an RTO of 3–7 minutes for control-plane recovery and session re-establishment; conservative customer-visible RTO of 5–15 minutes depending on client-side retry/backoff. RPO for model state (session context) is configurable; default is 0s for committed embeddings/context (we persist KV to a cross-region durable store every 30s for high-consistency customers) which yields an operational RPO of up to 30s.

- Scenario 2 (partial compute degradation): We prioritize low-latency traffic via dynamic routing and can autoscale into the standby pool; typical RTO is ~1–5 minutes for warm pools; RPO is 0s for committed writes and up to a few seconds for cached, best-effort in-memory prefixes.

- Scenario 3 (AZ storage degradation): Read-after-write semantics preserved for committed transactions (we use a quorum write path); RTO typically <10 minutes for degraded storage depending on provider repair time, and RPO is bounded by our commit window (configurable 0–60s).

I've attached: redwood_rto_rpo_matrix.xlsx (matrix with numeric fields and config knobs), arch-diagram-standby-region.png (high-level service flow), sla-fallback-matrix.pdf (policy-level choices we can commit to).

I'll loop in Marissa for technical elaboration on KV/cache behavior and Karthik to confirm our SLA language for procurement.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: regional standby / RTO-RPO mapping request — KV cache & consistency details

Hi Daniel — following up with the technical breakdown you requested. I pulled excerpts below and added a short runbook snippet.

KV cache & session state
- Active nodes keep an in-memory KV cache for low-latency context. That cache is asynchronously checkpointed to durable object storage every 30s by default. Customers can opt into synchronous checkpoints at commit points (recommended for strict RPO=0).
- During an automated region failover we route new requests to the standby region; client tokens are validated against the centralized auth service. For in-flight streaming sessions, the client must reconnect; our SDKs provide automatic transparent reconnect with progressive resume tokens — resume success rate ~98% in our tests.

Runbook excerpt (automated + manual steps)
1) Detection: health checks detect region-level outage; control plane escalates to standby policy.
2) Pre-warm: standbys receive traffic-shaping signals; model weights are kept cached in warm pools for priority customers.
3) Cutover: DNS TTLs and gateway routing adjusted; KV-store switched to cross-region leader where configured.
4) Manual hold: if there are stuck streaming contexts, SRE may run a reconciliation job (scripts provided) to drain/forward sessions — typical manual window <15 minutes.

Notes on observable impact
- Long-running streaming requests: If a client maintains a single TCP session, outage results in session drop; our recommended mitigation is SDK-level chunked checkpoints every 10s. This reduces worst-case lost context to ~10s.
- Write-before-commit: For customers who require strict distributed-transaction semantics, we support a synchronous commit option that incurs ~5–20ms extra latency on writes but guarantees cross-region durable write before acknowledgement.

I'll attach the CLI commands and the pre-built reconciliation job snippet from our ops repo if useful.

-Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks, this is helpful. A few follow-ups:
1) For scenario 1, can you confirm the assumptions behind the 3–7 minute control-plane recovery (are those assuming automated DNS failover or BGP-based routing?)
2) For synchronous checkpoint option, what's the operational impact on throughput for embeddings-heavy workloads (ballpark percent)?
3) Can you provide a short statement we can include in the RFP on whether Redwood will accept a multi-region read-only standby and the maximum replication lag we guarantee?

Procurement needs the answers for the RFP template — if you can reply with short bullets we'll paste them into the RFP.

Daniel
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@sentryfin.com>, rohan_mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T15:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: regional standby / RTO-RPO mapping request — official reply for procurement

Hi Daniel — quick bullets you can paste into the RFP template:

- Control-plane failover assumption: Our 3–7 minute control-plane RTO assumes an automated control-plane failover using our multi-region control-plane with DNS failover (we prefer low-TTL DNS combined with health-checked gateway updates; BGP-based routing is supported for enterprise customers via private connectivity and will reduce cutover to ~1–3 minutes where available).

- Synchronous checkpoint throughput impact: Enabling synchronous checkpoints for every commit can reduce peak throughput for embeddings-heavy bulk ingest by approximately 5–12% depending on region link latency; typical production customers see ~8% overhead at p95 traffic. Customers can use an adaptive policy (sync on critical commits, async for best-effort) to balance cost/latency.

- Multi-region read-only standby guarantee: We support a read-only standby configuration. Replication lag SLA for read-only standbys (when configured with our recommended durability profile) is documented as "typically <500ms; bounded under normal operating conditions to <2s". For contractual SLAs we can provide a replication-lag cap of 5s with associated routing and monitoring credits.

If you'd like, we can convert the bullets into a single short RFP paragraph and include the RTO/RPO matrix as an appendix.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect, Resilience | Redwood Inference
